title: A Compass for the Trail
premise: Orsen Underhill, who learned surveying and silence from her famous archaeologist father before walking away from him twelve years ago, is the only tracker skilled enough to find a vanished government survey team in the coastal badlands. Following their abandoned gear to a submerged wreck, she discovers the team didn't vanish—they were silenced by a salvage fleet captain who claims inheritance rights to the wreck through forged papers tied to her own family name. Racing six tides ahead of the fleet, Orsen must choose between claiming the legacy her father left buried there and destroying it to keep it out of corrupt hands; she sinks the evidence of the treasure itself, salvaging instead the truth—and an uneasy reconciliation with the father who taught her that some things are worth more found than kept.
about_author: August Ishikawa is a former marine cartographer who spent a decade charting coastlines from Hokkaido to the Aleutians before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who measure the world in distances they'd rather not cross emotionally.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Working a solitary contract mapping tidal flats, Orsen gets word that a government survey team has disappeared near territory she knows intimately—her father's old dig sites. She plans to refuse the search contract until she recognizes a piece of the abandoned gear as her father's design. Emotional beat: the pull of the past overriding twelve years of deliberate distance.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She reaches the survey camp: tents intact, instruments running, meals half-eaten, but no footprints leading out. Her expertise tells her the team left deliberately—or was taken by something that leaves no trace. She finds a logbook with coordinates circled in her father's handwriting style. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Wreck Beneath Six Tides
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, intercut with salvage captain Merrick Voss discovering her presence via a paid informant. The coordinates lead to a reef where low tides expose a wreck older than any registry—a vessel her father secretly excavated for years. Emotional beat: awe curdling into suspicion as she realizes someone else is already en route.

chapters.title: What Father Buried
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In a flooded sea cave she finds her father's hidden field notes: the wreck holds documents proving a colonial land-grant fraud that made powerful families wealthy—including, ambiguously, her own line. Emotional beat: the inheritance theme lands; legacy revealed as both gift and poison.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Aboard the flagship Corvane, Voss reveals his claim papers—forged through a complicit records office—and orders his crew to run Orsen down, framing her as the survey team's killer. Emotional beat: power shown as patient, bureaucratic corruption rather than open villainy.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Trail
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She encounters Ilya Renner, the survey team's sole survivor, hiding in the hills, wounded and hunted. He confirms Voss's men took the others. Distrust gives way to alliance over a shared fire. Emotional beat: love beginning against duty—Ilya wants justice; Orsen wants only to disappear again.

chapters.title: Six Tides Running
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With three tides left, she and Ilya race along the coast to reach the records vault in the port town before Voss's forged claim is filed. A betrayal by a harbormaster on Voss's payroll costs them their boat and nearly their lives. Emotional beat: desperation, and the first admission between them that failing together frightens less than failing alone.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Name
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Cornered, she sends for her father—the estranged archaeologist arrives, old and unrepentant, revealing he hid the documents to protect Orsen from the families who would kill for them. Their confrontation cracks twelve years of silence. Emotional beat: love against duty fully ignited; forgiveness offered but not yet accepted.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs converge at the reef. Voss's fleet arrives with the tide; Orsen triggers the collapse of the sea cave, burying the fraudulent grant forever while Ilya holds Voss's men at the cave mouth. Her father takes a bullet meant for her. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice, fury, and the irrevocable choice to destroy inheritance rather than be corrupted by it.

chapters.title: Compass True
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Voss is arrested when Ilya's testimony and the surviving survey logs expose him; her father survives, weakened, and asks nothing except to work beside her one last season. Orsen accepts—not a return to childhood, but something new. She stops measuring life in miles. Emotional beat: resolution—inheritance reclaimed as choice, love chosen over flight.
